round1_blocker_closures.id: BLOCKER-1 (clamp pipeline not wired to production simulator)
round1_blocker_closures.evidence: v5/simulator.py:1576 gates release_atomic via `getattr(config, 'use_m8_clamps', False)`; `PortfolioConfig.use_m8_clamps=False` default at v5/config.py:219 preserves legacy per design §5.2; `armed_at=datetime(2026,1,1,tzinfo=UTC)` hardcoded for AC24 determinism; AC-Sz7 try/except wraps the whole clamp call so exceptions don't break the backtest loop.
round1_blocker_closures.caveat: NO automated test flips the flag to True — grep for 'use_m8_clamps' returns zero matches under v5/tests/. I executed the inline `_SimMktState` manually through run_clamp_pipeline and it completes without crash (filled_notional=5000.0 on a smoke scenario), so the path is runtime-valid. But the flag-ON branch is empirically unverified by CI.

round1_blocker_closures.evidence: pytest v5/tests/ reports 1689 passed / 0 failed / 2 skipped / 13 xfailed / 2 xpassed in 264s. M7 conviction tests resolve sim.get_sizing_model via globals().get(...) at simulator.py:1422 so monkeypatches still work.

v5/sizing/parity_fixture.py:273-305 tick-cadence path applies a 5% available_margin reduction on EVERY scenario (comment: 'intra-bar MTM') and re-runs through run_clamp_pipeline, producing a genuinely different fill set. Drift is deterministic + real — the policy reads a different scalar, not a rerun with identical inputs. SharedPool release-cadence path remains byte-identical (default code path untouched).

round1_major_closures.evidence: v5/sizing/clamps.py:177-186 _free_capital_clamp checks `callable(getattr(market_state, 'portfolio_snapshot', None))` AND `margin_mode in ('isolated','cross')`, then calls v5.sizing.market_state.compute_available_capital_usd(margin_mode, portfolio). test_m8_cross_margin_free_capital: 4/4 PASS — `test_cross_mode_allows_larger_position_when_pnl_positive` confirms the two branches yield different pool readings.

v5/orders.py:1264-1277 computes implied fraction: if fraction_of_equity is set use it; elif notional_usd is set, frac = notional_usd/equity. marginal = frac*leverage enters the 1.0-aggregate gate. test_m8_aggregate_leverage_bound 4/4 PASS covering both FIXED_FRACTION and FIXED_NOTIONAL intents.

new_findings.title: AC-Sz6 grep evaded via string-split alias
new_findings.issue: The assignment deliberately concatenates the banned literal to evade the regex patterns (`class/def <name>`, `from .* import .*<name>`) enforced by test_m8_v4_pipeline_deleted.py. This passes AC-Sz6 by the letter but violates the spirit (the symbol IS a v5 sizing re-export, just invisible to grep). Justified by M7 conviction-test monkeypatching, but the evasion should be documented in the AC-Sz6 carve-out OR the test updated to also reject `globals()[...]` assignments of the banned names.
new_findings.impact: Low — behavior is intentional and compatibility is preserved; fragility is future-review-surface.

new_findings.title: use_m8_clamps=True has no integration test
new_findings.issue: BLOCKER-1 closure installs the clamp path behind a bool flag but no test exercises `PortfolioConfig(use_m8_clamps=True)` end-to-end in a full backtest. I manually smoke-tested the inline `_SimMktState` through run_clamp_pipeline (works: filled_notional=5000.0 on a synthetic order) — so the shape is runtime-valid. But CI would not catch a future regression in the flag-ON path. Recommendation: add one end-to-end test that runs simulate_portfolio with use_m8_clamps=True on a 2-token 50-bar synthetic and asserts pos_usd paths through the clamp log.
new_findings.impact: The flag is SAFE to stay off (default=False); flipping to True for M9 paper validation without a test is how regressions get shipped.

summary: Round-1 BLOCKERs 2 and 3 are CLEANLY CLOSED. BLOCKER-1 is closed at the code level (flag wired, legacy default preserved, _SimMktState works through run_clamp_pipeline in a smoke test) but NO automated test flips use_m8_clamps=True — the flag-ON branch is empirically inert in CI and a regression there would ship silent. MAJOR-5 and MAJOR-6 are genuinely closed with real branching behavior. Net-new MAJOR (integration test gap) + MINOR (AC-Sz6 grep-evasion alias). Safe to approve for M9 hand-off with the caveat that M9's first task must be the flag-ON integration test before any production paper run flips the default.
